contract: The no-C-compiler job is expected to FAIL while this list is non-empty, and expected to fail ONLY for reasons on it. A failure whose reason is absent here is a regression, not progress. The list is the phase's schedule: it shrinks patch by patch, and the job becomes required when it empties -- by a patch that says so, never automatically.

entries.reason: rustc uses cc as its linker driver on *-linux-gnu, including for the musl self-contained target, so a C-free link needs -C linker=rust-lld explicitly.
entries.cleared_by: 25.11 -- cc optional, musl + rust-lld proved here
entries.observable_note: Newly observable, and it is the FIRST failure on a clean checkout: cargo builds the native backend before anything links, and rustc invokes cc for its build scripts. Measured by Patch 25.10 from CI, not locally -- a tree with build/gust-native-backend already present gets past this and fails at the link step instead, which is a different entry.

patch2512b_measurement.finding: NOT specific to gnu. Measured on a musl HOST (rust:alpine, C compilers shadowed off PATH): `cargo build` of a trivial crate fails with `error: linker \`cc\` not found` -- this entry's own observable_signature. rustc defaults to cc as its linker driver on musl hosts too.
patch2512b_measurement.consequence: Changing the falsifier's IMAGE cannot clear this. It is cleared by configuring the linker explicitly, which scripts/phase25_musl_c_free_link.py proves works: -C linker=rust-lld -C linker-flavor=ld.lld against the musl target links, runs and is static-pie.
patch2512b_measurement.why_the_workload_still_fails: WORKLOAD is ['make','gust'], which cargo-builds the Cranelift backend. Building it for musl with cc poisoned fails in libm's BUILD SCRIPT -- a HOST binary linked for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- because cargo builds build scripts for the host regardless of --target. Patch 25.11 measured that gnu + rust-lld has no C-free link at all (-lc -lm -ldl -lpthread -lrt -lutil -lgcc_s unfound), so on a gnu host this cannot be configured away.
patch2512b_measurement.what_would_clear_it: A musl HOST for the no-C job, plus an explicit rust-lld linker configuration so the default never applies. Both halves are needed: the host alone does not (measured above), and the configuration alone does not (build scripts are host-linked).

entries.reason: The Cranelift backend links its objects by spawning a C driver: compiler/experiments/cranelift/src/main.rs:16533 reads `env::var_os("CC").unwrap_or_else(|| "cc")`. Removing C COMPILATION from the tree does not remove C LINKING from the native route.
entries.measured_by: Patch 25.10, by running the workload after the bootstrap chain was deleted
entries.cleared_by: an internal or non-cc link step for the native backend -- lld, or a linker invoked directly rather than through a C driver. Not by any further C deletion, because there is no C left to delete on this path.
entries.observable_note: Observable only once the native backend is already built. On a clean no-C checkout rustc-defaults-to-cc-on-gnu fires first, so this is the SECOND barrier on that path, not the first. Both are real; they are different programs reaching for cc -- rustc for its build scripts, and the Gust backend for its own link step.

patch2512b_measurement.finding: The mechanism is more tractable than the entry implies. There are only TWO CompilerMirLinkRequest constructors, and the executor is a generic command builder that already carries additional_linker_args -- so a non-cc linker is EXPRESSIBLE without rewriting it. The hardcoding is one line: main.rs:16532.
patch2512b_measurement.the_real_obstacle: Not the plumbing, the link LINE. A direct rust-lld invocation must supply the self-contained crt objects AND enumerate Rust's std rlibs (libstd, libpanic_unwind, libobject, libmemchr, libaddr2line, libgimli, libcfg_if, librustc_demangle, libstd_detect, libhashbrown, librustc_std_workspace_alloc, libminiz_oxide, libadler2, libunwind, liblibc, libcore, liballoc, libcompiler_builtins), because the Gust runtime archive is Rust and depends on std. rustc computes that set; reproducing it in the backend is version-fragile.
two_designs: Reimplement the link line: the backend enumerates crt objects and std rlibs from `rustc --print sysroot`. Self-contained but breaks whenever rustc's std layout moves.

Link THROUGH rustc with -C linker=rust-lld: rustc computes the rlibs, and no C compiler is involved anywhere. Needs the backend to emit a shim crate rather than hand raw objects to a linker, which is an architectural change.
patch2512b_measurement.not_attempted_here: Patch 25.12b measured this and stopped rather than ship an unverifiable half-implementation. The backend has ZERO musl/lld/linker-flavor awareness across 37,338 lines of main.rs; this is a feature, not a patch.

excepted.reason: Editor tooling. Makefile:262 test target never names test_tree_sitter, no workflow mentions it, and the only routes are explicit opt-in. Optional under D10, so out of scope rather than on the schedule.

cleared.reason_when_recorded: src/runtime/*.c is 1,968 hand-written lines compiled by $(CC); every binary links it.
cleared.cleared_by: Patch 25.12b, on the criterion this phase wrote for it
evidence: src/runtime/*.c is 0 files -- this entry's own patch2510a_measurement already recorded src_runtime_c_files: 0.

docs/PHASE25_ROADMAP.md and src/runtime-rs/src/strings.rs both state the condition in the same words: 'neither is cleared while $(CC) compiles strings.c into build/gust-runtime-package.a'. PHASE21_RUNTIME_OBJECTS is EMPTY, the package rule is `ar rcs` over the Rust object alone, and no $(CC) rule feeds it.
WORKLOAD is ['make','gust'], and the gust: target references neither src/runtime.c nor $(CC), so this entry cannot describe a failure of the measured workload.
It carried NO observable_signature, so it could never match an observed failure -- it held the gate closed only by counting toward len(entries).
cleared.what_survives: src/runtime.c: 2 effective lines (two #includes) plus 27 lines of history. It is a PRESERVED_BOUNDARIES marker that scripts/phase19_retired_prototype_absence.py REQUIRES to exist, and 98 tracked files name it. Deleting it is a separate change and is not what this entry claimed.
cleared.not_cleared_with_it: runtime-archive-is-glibc-bound shares the older prose above, but Patch 25.10a re-scoped it: the remaining symbols come from Rust's std, so it needs a musl Rust target and is NOT cleared by removing C.

cleared.reason_when_recorded: build/gust-runtime-package.a carries glibc-only undefined symbols, so it cannot link against musl and the C-free link cannot be proved.
cleared.cleared_by: Patch 25.12b, by the musl Rust target its own cleared_by named
evidence: The entry's cleared_by: 'Clearing it needs a musl Rust target (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl), because the remaining symbols come from Rust's std.' That is exactly what was done.

scripts/phase25_musl_c_free_link.py builds the runtime crate for x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, links a program that CALLS gust_tick through rust-lld with cc/gcc/clang/c++/g++/cc1/ld/ld.gold/ld.bfd all poisoned to exit 99, runs it, and requires exit 7 and no INTERP segment.

Patch 25.11 had measured 'musl + rust-lld + ld.lld flavor WORKS: static-pie, exit 7' but could not include the runtime archive, and said so: 'THE GATE IS NOT PROVABLE UNTIL THE RUNTIME STOPS BEING C'. 25.5, 25.6 and 25.10a finished that; PHASE21_RUNTIME_OBJECTS is empty and the archive is ar rcs over one Rust object.
The five glibc symbols this entry named -- __printf_chk, __fprintf_chk, __memcpy_chk, __isoc23_strtol, __stack_chk -- are absent from the musl archive (nm --undefined-only: 0 each).

MUTATION-TESTED: with nothing poisoned the guard refuses to certify ('the poisoned cc did not fire'); with the archive off the link path it fails 'unable to find library'. Baseline restores byte-identical.
cleared.what_this_does_not_claim: NOT that `make gust` is C-free on gnu. Patch 25.11 decided the user default stays the host target (O6) and that a gnu host with no C compiler ERRORS naming musl rather than silently switching (P10). 25.11 measured that no stock C-free link exists on gnu at all. This is the musl proof the phase always said it would be.
